indicativo.title: Indicativo
indicativo.summary: The mood of facts: what happens, happened or will happen.
body: The indicative presents something as real or certain. It is the default mood of Italian: unless something calls for another mood, the verb is in the indicative.

head: Tense
Example
Expresses
rows: Now, habits, general truths, the near future
Past habits, descriptions, actions in progress
Completed actions cut off from the present, narrative
The future, guesses about the present
Before another future moment, guesses about the past

body: Each compound tense is the auxiliary *avere* or *essere* in the matching simple tense, plus the past participle.
Verbs of knowing and stating take the indicative: *So che {ip:parla} bene.* Opinions, wishes and doubts take the subjunctive: *Penso che {csp:parli} bene.*

presente.title: Presente
presente.summary: What is happening now, what usually happens, and often the near future.
body: Remove *-are*, *-ere* or *-ire* and add the endings. Many *-ire* verbs insert *-isc-* everywhere except in *noi* and *voi*: *capire, finire, preferire, pulire, spedire*.
Verbs in *-care* and *-gare* add an *h* to keep the hard sound: *cerchi, paghiamo*. Verbs in *-ciare* and *-giare* keep a single *i*: *cominci, mangiamo*.

ul: Something happening now: *Adesso {ip:leggo} il giornale.*
Habits: *Il lunedì {ip:vado} in palestra.*
General truths: *L'acqua {ip:bolle} a cento gradi.*
The near future, usually with a time word: *Domani {ip:parto} per Roma.*
An action that began in the past and still continues, with *da*: *{ip:Studio} italiano da due anni.*

imperfetto.title: Imperfetto
imperfetto.summary: The past seen from the inside: habits, descriptions and actions in progress.
body: Remove *-re* from the infinitive and add *-vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano*. It is the most regular tense in Italian.
Only *essere* is truly irregular. *Fare, dire, bere* and verbs in *-urre* use their longer Latin stem.

ul: Past habits: *Da bambino {im:andavo} al mare ogni estate.*
Descriptions of people, places, weather and states: *{im:Era} tardi e {im:pioveva}.*
An action in progress when something else happened: *{im:Dormivo} quando {pp:è arrivato} Marco.*
Two actions going on at the same time: *Mentre {im:cucinavo}, lui {im:apparecchiava}.*
Polite requests: *{im:Volevo} un caffè, per favore.*

body: The [im:imperfetto] shows the background or a state with no clear end. The [pp:passato prossimo] shows a completed event: *{im:Faceva} freddo, così {pp:ho chiuso} la finestra.*

passato_prossimo.title: Passato prossimo
body: Use the present of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle: *-are* becomes *-ato*, *-ere* becomes *-uto*, *-ire* becomes *-ito*.

ul: Most verbs take *avere*, including every verb with a direct object.
*Essere* goes with verbs of movement or change of state and no object: *andare, venire, partire, arrivare, uscire, entrare, nascere, morire, diventare*.
*Essere* also goes with *essere, stare, restare, rimanere, piacere* and all reflexive verbs: *mi {pp:sono alzato}*.

body: With *essere* the participle agrees with the subject: *Lei {pp:è andat**a**}.* With *avere* it stays in *-o*, unless the object is *lo, la, li, le*: *L'{pp:ho vist**a**}.*

ul: Completed actions, with words like *ieri* or *la settimana scorsa*: *Ieri {pp:ho visto} un film.*
A sequence of events: *{pp:Mi sono alzato}, {pp:ho fatto} colazione e {pp:sono uscito}.*
Past events that still matter now: *{pp:Ho perso} le chiavi.*
An event that interrupts an action in progress: *{im:Dormivo} quando {pp:ha suonato} il telefono.*

trapassato_prossimo.title: Trapassato prossimo
body: Use the [im:imperfetto] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle. The same rules for the auxiliary and agreement apply as in the [pp:passato prossimo].

ul: An action completed before another past event: *Quando {pp:sono arrivato}, il treno {tp:era già partito}.*
The cause of a past situation: *{im:Ero} stanco perché {tp:avevo lavorato} tutto il giorno.*
Reported speech about something earlier: *Ha detto che {tp:aveva finito}.*
First-time experiences: *Non {tp:avevo mai visto} una cosa simile.*

passato_remoto.title: Passato remoto
passato_remoto.summary: Completed actions cut off from the present, above all in books and history.
body: Remove *-are*, *-ere* or *-ire* and add the endings. Regular *-ere* verbs also have a longer alternative in *-etti, -ette, -ettero*.
Many verbs are irregular only in *io*, *lui / lei* and *loro*. The other three persons are regular. *Essere* is irregular throughout.
Also: *vedere: vidi; prendere: presi; venire: venni; dire: dissi; sapere: seppi; volere: volli; leggere: lessi; mettere: misi; nascere: nacqui.*

ul: Historical events: *Dante {pr:nacque} a Firenze nel 1265.*
Narrative in novels and tales, with the [im:imperfetto] as background: *{im:Era} notte quando {pr:bussarono} alla porta.*
In speech it is common mainly in parts of southern Italy. Elsewhere speakers normally use the [pp:passato prossimo].

trapassato_remoto.title: Trapassato remoto
trapassato_remoto.summary: A rare literary tense: one action just before another in the [pr:passato remoto].
body: Use the [pr:passato remoto] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle.
It appears only in subordinate clauses after *dopo che*, *appena*, *non appena* or *quando*, and the main verb is in the [pr:passato remoto].

ul: *Appena {tr:ebbe finito}, {pr:uscì}.*
*Dopo che {tr:furono partiti}, la casa {pr:rimase} vuota.*

body: You only need to recognise it. In everyday Italian, say *Dopo aver finito, è uscito.*

futuro_semplice.title: Futuro semplice
futuro_semplice.summary: What will happen, and guesses about the present.
body: Remove the final *-e* of the infinitive and add *-ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno*.
⚠️ In *-are* verbs the *a* becomes *e*.
Spelling: *cercare: cercherò; pagare: pagherò; cominciare: comincerò; mangiare: mangerò.*
The endings stay the same. Only the stem changes.

ul: Future events and plans: *L'anno prossimo {fs:andremo} in Giappone.*
Promises and predictions: *Te lo {ip:prometto}: {fs:tornerò}.*
A guess about the present: *Che ore sono? {fs:Saranno} le otto.*
After *se* and *quando* when the event is in the future: *Quando {fs:arriverai}, ti {fs:mostrerò} la casa.*

futuro_anteriore.title: Futuro anteriore
futuro_anteriore.summary: What will already have happened, and guesses about the past.
body: Use the [fs:futuro semplice] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle.

ul: An action finished before another future one, after *quando, dopo che, appena*: *Quando {fa:avrò finito}, ti {fs:chiamerò}.*
A guess about the past: *Non è ancora qui: {fa:avrà perso} il treno.*

condizionale.title: Condizionale
condizionale.summary: The mood of what would happen: politeness, advice, wishes and hypotheses.
body: The conditional presents an action as dependent on a condition or softens what is said. It has two tenses.

head: Tense
Example
Refers to
rows: The past, or a future seen from the past

body: The *se* clause takes the *congiuntivo*, never the conditional. The conditional goes in the result clause.

ul: Possible now: *Se {csi:avessi} tempo, {cop:viaggerei}.*
Impossible, in the past: *Se {cst:avessi avuto} tempo, {cpa:avrei viaggiato}.*
Past condition, present result: *Se {cst:avessi studiato}, ora {cop:saprei} la risposta.*

condizionale_presente.title: Condizionale presente
condizionale_presente.summary: Would do: polite requests, advice, wishes, hypotheses.
body: Take the stem of the [fs:futuro semplice] and add *-ei, -esti, -ebbe, -emmo, -este, -ebbero*. Note *-emmo* with a double *m*: the future has *-emo*.
They are the same as in the future: {cop:sarei}, {cop:avrei}, {cop:andrei}, {cop:farei}, {cop:potrei}, {cop:dovrei}, {cop:saprei}, {cop:vorrei}, {cop:verrei}, {cop:berrei}.

ul: Polite requests: *{cop:Vorrei} un caffè. {cop:Potrebbe} aiutarmi?*
Advice: *{cop:Dovresti} dormire di più.*
Wishes: *Mi {cop:piacerebbe} vivere al mare.*
The result of a hypothesis: *Se {csi:potessi}, {cop:partirei} subito.*
Unconfirmed news: *Il ministro {cop:sarebbe} a Parigi.*

condizionale_passato.title: Condizionale passato
condizionale_passato.summary: Would have done, and the future seen from the past.
body: Use the [cop:condizionale presente] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle.

ul: A result that did not happen: *Se {cst:avessi studiato}, {cpa:avrei passato} l'esame.*
A wish or intention that was not fulfilled: *{cpa:Sarei venuto}, ma {im:ero} malato.*
Regret or criticism: *{cpa:Avresti dovuto} dirmelo.*
The future seen from the past. English says *would come*, Italian needs the compound form: *Ha detto che {cpa:sarebbe venuto}.*
Unconfirmed past news: *Il ladro {cpa:sarebbe fuggito} in auto.*

imperativo.title: Imperativo
imperativo.summary: Commands, requests, advice and instructions, for every way of addressing someone.

head: Form
Used for
rows: Several people, very formally; usually replaced by *voi*

body: The *tu* form of *-are* verbs ends in *-a*, and of the others in *-i*. *Noi* and *voi* match the present. *Lei* and *Loro* are borrowed from the [csp:congiuntivo presente], so the vowels swap: *-are* verbs take *-i*, the others *-a*.
Only *tu* changes: *non* plus the infinitive. The other persons simply add *non*.
With *tu*, *noi* and *voi* the pronoun joins the end of the verb. With *Lei* and *Loro* it stays in front. In the negative of *tu*, *noi* and *voi* it can go in either place.
Object pronouns follow the same rule as reflexive ones.

ul: *{imv:Chiamami!}* (tu), *Mi {imv:chiami!}* (Lei), *{imv:Chiamatemi!}* (voi), *Non {imv:chiamarmi!}* (tu)
Two pronouns together: *{imv:Dammelo!}*, *{imv:Diglielo!}*, *Me lo {imv:dia!}*

body: After the short forms *va', fa', da', sta', di'* the first consonant of the pronoun doubles: *{imv:Dammi}, {imv:Fallo}, {imv:Dimmi}, {imv:Vacci}, {imv:Stammi} a sentire.* The only exception is *gli*: *{imv:Digli}*.

ul: Commands: *{imv:Chiudi} la porta!*
Requests, softened with *per favore*: *Mi {imv:passi} il sale, per favore.*
Advice: *{imv:Riposati} un po'.*
Invitations: *{imv:Venite} a cena da noi!*
Written instructions often use the infinitive instead: *Non calpestare le aiuole.*

congiuntivo.title: Congiuntivo
congiuntivo.summary: The mood of what is thought, wished, feared or doubted, rather than stated as fact.
body: The subjunctive presents something as subjective or uncertain. It appears mostly in subordinate clauses introduced by *che*, or after certain conjunctions.

ul: Opinions: *Penso che {csp:sia} vero.*
Wishes and requests: *Voglio che tu {csp:venga}.*
Doubt: *Non so se {csp:abbia} ragione.*
Emotions: *Sono felice che tu {csp:sia} qui.*
Impersonal expressions: *Bisogna che {csp:parta}. È importante che {csp:capiscano}.*
After *benché, sebbene, affinché, prima che, purché, a meno che, senza che*.
Relative clauses after a superlative or an indefinite: *È il libro più bello che {csa:abbia letto}.*
Hypotheses with *se*: *Se {csi:potessi}, {cop:verrei}.*

body: It is not used after *so che*, *sono sicuro che*, *è vero che* or *perché* meaning because.
The tense depends on the verb in the main clause and on whether the action comes at the same time or earlier.

congiuntivo_presente.title: Congiuntivo presente
congiuntivo_presente.summary: Thoughts, wishes and doubts about now or the future.
body: *-are* verbs take *-i*, the others take *-a*. The three singular persons are identical, so *io, tu, lui* are often needed for clarity.
Also: *dare: dia; stare: stia; sapere: sappia; potere: possa; volere: voglia; dovere: debba; venire: venga; dire: dica; uscire: esca.*
It follows a main verb in the present or future and refers to the same time or later.

ul: *Credo che {csp:arrivi} domani.*
*Spero che tu {csp:stia} bene.*
*Benché {csp:piova}, esco.*
*Ti aiuto affinché tu {csp:possa} finire.*

congiuntivo_passato.title: Congiuntivo passato
congiuntivo_passato.summary: Thoughts and feelings now about something that has already happened.
body: Use the [csp:congiuntivo presente] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle.
The main verb is in the present and the action in the subjunctive came earlier.

ul: *Credo che {csa:abbia dimenticato}.*
*Sono contento che tu {csa:sia venuto}.*
*Benché {csa:abbia studiato}, non {pp:ha passato} l'esame.*
*È il film più bello che {csa:abbia visto}.*

congiuntivo_imperfetto.title: Congiuntivo imperfetto
congiuntivo_imperfetto.summary: The subjunctive after a past verb, in hypotheses and in wishes.
body: Remove *-re* from the infinitive and add *-ssi, -ssi, -sse, -ssimo, -ste, -ssero*.
Also, with the same stem as the [im:imperfetto]: *dire: dicessi; bere: bevessi; tradurre: traducessi.*

ul: After a main verb in a past tense: *Pensavo che {csi:fosse} Perugia.*
After a conditional: *Vorrei che tu {csi:restassi}.*
Hypotheses that are unlikely or unreal now: *Se {csi:avessi} tempo, {cop:leggerei} di più.*
Wishes: *Magari {csi:potessi} venire!*
After *come se*: *Parla come se {csi:sapesse} tutto.*

congiuntivo_trapassato.title: Congiuntivo trapassato
congiuntivo_trapassato.summary: The earlier past in the subjunctive, and hypotheses that can no longer come true.
body: Use the [csi:congiuntivo imperfetto] of *avere* or *essere* and the past participle.

ul: An action before a past main verb: *Pensavo che {cst:fosse partito}.*
Past hypotheses that did not come true: *Se {cst:avessi saputo}, {cpa:sarei venuto}.*
Regrets: *Magari ti {cst:avessi ascoltato}!*
After *come se*: *Mi guarda come se non mi {cst:avesse mai visto}.*
